data: © Soviet Academy of Sciences (historical) — landing site approximate, NSSDCA catalogue.

First human-built object to reach the Martian surface — by impact. The lander's parachute failed during EDL on 27 November 1971; it crashed at high speed in the Hellas region. The orbiter component continued to return data for eight months. Mars 2 began the Soviet attempt to leapfrog the Americans to the Martian surface in the 1971 launch window.
Demonstrated that reaching Mars's surface — even by impact — was achievable in a single launch window.

On 27 November 1971, a few hours before Mars 2 entered orbit, its descent capsule separated and headed for the surface. The descent system failed — probably because the capsule came in too steeply — the parachute did not open, and it struck the ground: the first human-made object to reach the surface of Mars. Inside was PrOP-M, a small rover built to walk on skis at the end of a tether. The orbiter worked on into 1972.
27 November 1971 — the first object on Mars
The 1972 Soviet stamp for the Mars 2 automatic station: the pennant it carried reached the planet on 27 November 1971.
A museum model of the Mars 3 descent module — Mars 2 carried the same design. Mars 3 landed softly five days later and sent a signal for 14.5 seconds.
